NKJV.1: Behold, you are fair, my love! Behold, you are fair! You have dove’s eyes behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats, Going down from Mount Gilead.
NKJV.2: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep Which have come up from the washing, Every one of which bears twins, And none is barren among them.
NKJV.3: Your lips are like a strand of scarlet, And your mouth is lovely. Your temples behind your veil Are like a piece of pomegranate.
NKJV.4: Your neck is like the tower of David, Built for an armory, On which hang a thousand bucklers, All shields of mighty men.
NKJV.5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle, Which feed among the lilies.
NKJV.6: Until the day breaks And the shadows flee away, I will go my way to the mountain of myrrh And to the hill of frankincense.
NKJV.7: You are all fair, my love, And there is no spot in you.
NKJV.8: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, With me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, From the mountains of the leopards.
NKJV.9: You have ravished my heart, My sister, my spouse; You have ravished my heart With one look of your eyes, With one link of your necklace.
NKJV.10: How fair is your love, My sister, my spouse! How much better than wine is your love, And the scent of your perfumes Than all spices!
NKJV.11: Your lips, O my spouse, Drip as the honeycomb; Honey and milk are under your tongue; And the fragrance of your garments Is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
NKJV.12: A garden enclosed Is my sister, my spouse, A spring shut up, A fountain sealed.
NKJV.13: Your plants are an orchard of pomegranates With pleasant fruits, Fragrant henna with spikenard,
NKJV.14: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, With all trees of frankincense, Myrrh and aloes, With all the chief spices—
NKJV.15: A fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And streams from Lebanon.
NKJV.16: Awake, O north wind, And come, O south! Blow upon my garden, That its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come to his garden And eat its pleasant fruits.

ESV.1: Behold, you are beautiful, my love, behold, you are beautiful! Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats leaping down the slopes of Gilead.
ESV.2: Your teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes that have come up from the washing, all of which bear twins, and not one among them has lost its young.
ESV.3: Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your mouth is lovely. Your cheeks are like halves of a pomegranate behind your veil.
ESV.4: Your neck is like the tower of David, built in rows of stone;  on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
ESV.5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that graze among the lilies.
ESV.6: Until the day breathes and the shadows flee, I will go away to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
ESV.7: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.
ESV.8: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride; come with me from Lebanon. Depart  from the peak of Amana, from the peak of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
ESV.9: You have captivated my heart, my sister, my bride; you have captivated my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
ESV.10: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, and the fragrance of your oils than any spice!
ESV.11: Your lips drip nectar, my bride; honey and milk are under your tongue; the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
ESV.12: A garden locked is my sister, my bride, a spring locked, a fountain sealed.
ESV.13: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with all choicest fruits, henna with nard,
ESV.14: nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all choice spices —
ESV.15: a garden fountain, a well of living water, and flowing streams from Lebanon.
ESV.16: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind! Blow upon my garden, let its spices flow. Together in the Garden of Love She Let my beloved come to his garden, and eat its choicest fruits.

NLT.1:
You are beautiful, my darling,
beautiful beyond words.
Your eyes are like doves
behind your veil.
Your hair falls in waves,
like a flock of goats winding down the slopes of Gilead.
NLT.2:
Your teeth are as white as sheep,
recently shorn and freshly washed.
Your smile is flawless,
each tooth matched with its twin.
NLT.3:
Your lips are like scarlet ribbon;
your mouth is inviting.
Your cheeks are like rosy pomegranates
behind your veil.
NLT.4:
Your neck is as beautiful as the tower of David,
jeweled with the shields of a thousand heroes.
NLT.5:
Your breasts are like two fawns,
twin fawns of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
NLT.6:
Before the dawn breezes blow
and the night shadows flee,
I will hurry to the mountain of myrrh
and to the hill of frankincense.
NLT.7:
You are altogether beautiful, my darling,
beautiful in every way.
NLT.8:
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride,
come with me from Lebanon.
Come down from Mount Amana,
from the peaks of Senir and Hermon,
where the lions have their dens
and leopards live among the hills.
NLT.9:
You have captured my heart,
my treasure, my bride.
You hold it hostage with one glance of your eyes,
with a single jewel of your necklace.
NLT.10:
Your love delights me,
my treasure, my bride.
Your love is better than wine,
your perfume more fragrant than spices.
NLT.11:
Your lips are as sweet as nectar, my bride.
Honey and milk are under your tongue.
Your clothes are scented
like the cedars of Lebanon.
NLT.12:
You are my private garden, my treasure, my bride,
a secluded spring, a hidden fountain.
NLT.13:
Your thighs shelter a paradise of pomegranates
with rare spices —
henna with nard,
NLT.14:
nard and saffron,
fragrant calamus and cinnamon,
with all the trees of frankincense, myrrh, and aloes,
and every other lovely spice.
NLT.15:
You are a garden fountain,
a well of fresh water
streaming down from Lebanon’s mountains.
NLT.16:
Awake, north wind!
Rise up, south wind!
Blow on my garden
and spread its fragrance all around.
Come into your garden, my love;
taste its finest fruits.

AMP.1:
(The Bridegroom) "How fair and beautiful you are, my darling,
How very beautiful!
Your eyes behind your veil are like those of a dove;
Your hair is like [the shimmering black fleece of] a flock of [Arabian] goats
That have descended from Mount Gilead [beyond the Jordan].
AMP.2:
"Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn ewes
Which have come up from washing,
All of which bear twins,
And not one among them has lost her young.
AMP.3:
"Your lips are like a ribbon of scarlet,
And your mouth is lovely.
Your temples are like a slice of the pomegranate
Behind your veil.
AMP.4:
"Your neck is like the tower of David,
Built with rows of [glistening] stones,
Whereon hang a thousand shields,
All of them shields of warriors.
AMP.5:
"Your two breasts are like two fawns,
Twins of a gazelle
Which feed among the lilies.
AMP.6:
"Until the day breaks
And the shadows flee away,
[In my thoughts] I will go my way to the mountain of myrrh
And to the hill of frankincense.
AMP.7:
"O my love, you are altogether beautiful and fair.
There is no flaw nor blemish in you!
AMP.8:
"Come away with me from Lebanon, my [promised] bride,
May you come with me from Lebanon.
Journey down from the top of Amana,
From the summit of Senir and Hermon,
From the dens of lions,
From the mountains of leopards.
AMP.9:
"You have ravished my heart and given me courage, my sister, my [promised] bride;
You have ravished my heart and given me courage with a single glance of your eyes,
With one jewel of your necklace.
AMP.10:
"How beautiful is your love, my sister, my [promised] bride!
How much better is your love than wine,
And the fragrance of your oils
Than all kinds of balsam and spices.
AMP.11:
"Your lips, my [promised] bride, drip honey [as the honeycomb];
Honey and milk are under your tongue,
And the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
AMP.12:
"A garden enclosed is my sister, my [promised] bride—
A rock garden locked, a spring sealed up.
AMP.13:
"Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates,
[A paradise] with precious fruits, henna with fragrant plants,
AMP.14:
Fragrant plants and saffron, calamus and cinnamon,
With all trees of frankincense,
Myrrh and aloes, along with all the finest spices.
AMP.15:
"You are a fountain in a garden,
A well of fresh and living water,
And streams flowing from Lebanon."
AMP.16:
(The Shulammite Bride) "Awake, O north wind,
And come, south wind [blow softly upon my garden];
Make my garden breathe out fragrance, [for the one in whom my soul delights],
Let its spices flow forth.
Let my beloved come into his garden
And eat its choicest fruits."

By your hair as it flows and shimmers,
like a flock of goats in the distance
streaming down a hillside in the sunshine.
MSG.2:
Your smile is generous and full—
expressive and strong and clean.
MSG.3:
Your lips are jewel red,
your mouth elegant and inviting,
your veiled cheeks soft and radiant.
MSG.4:
The smooth, lithe lines of your neck
command notice—all heads turn in awe and admiration!
MSG.5:
Your breasts are like fawns,
twins of a gazelle, grazing among the first spring flowers.
MSG.6:
The sweet, fragrant curves of your body,
the soft, spiced contours of your flesh
Invite me, and I come. I stay
until dawn breathes its light and night slips away.
MSG.7:
You're beautiful from head to toe, my dear love,
beautiful beyond compare, absolutely flawless.
MSG.8:
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride.
Leave Lebanon behind, and come.
Leave your high mountain hideaway.
Abandon your wilderness seclusion,
Where you keep company with lions
and panthers guard your safety.
MSG.9:
You've captured my heart, dear friend.
You looked at me, and I fell in love.
One look my way and I was hopelessly in love!
MSG.10:
How beautiful your love, dear, dear friend—
far more pleasing than a fine, rare wine,
your fragrance more exotic than select spices.
MSG.11:
The kisses of your lips are honey, my love,
every syllable you speak a delicacy to savor.
Your clothes smell like the wild outdoors,
the ozone scent of high mountains.
MSG.12:
Dear lover and friend, you're a secret garden,
a private and pure fountain.
MSG.13:
Body and soul, you are paradise,
a whole orchard of succulent fruits—
Ripe apricots and peaches,
oranges and pears;
Nut trees and cinnamon,
and all scented woods;
MSG.14:
Mint and lavender,
and all herbs aromatic;
MSG.15:
A garden fountain, sparkling and splashing,
fed by spring waters from the Lebanon mountains.
MSG.16:
Wake up, North Wind,
get moving, South Wind!
Breathe on my garden,
fill the air with spice fragrance.
Oh, let my lover enter his garden!
Yes, let him eat the fine, ripe fruits.

NET.1: Oh, you are beautiful, my darling! Oh, you are beautiful! Your eyes behind your veil are like doves. Your hair is like a flock of female goats descending from Mount Gilead.
NET.2: Your teeth are like a flock of newly-shorn sheep coming up from the washing place; each of them has a twin, and not one of them is missing.
NET.3: Your lips are like a scarlet thread; your mouth is lovely. Your forehead behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
NET.4: Your neck is like the tower of David built with courses of stones; one thousand shields are hung on it — all shields of valiant warriors.
NET.5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of the gazelle grazing among the lilies.
NET.6: Until the dawn arrives and the shadows flee, I will go up to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
NET.7: You are altogether beautiful, my darling! There is no blemish in you!
NET.8: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Descend from the crest of Amana, from the top of Senir, the summit of Hermon, from the lions’ dens and the mountain haunts of the leopards.
NET.9: You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride! You have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your necklace.
NET.10: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine; the fragrance of your perfume is better than any spice!
NET.11: Your lips drip sweetness like the honeycomb, my bride, honey and milk are under your tongue. The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
NET.12: You are a locked garden, my sister, my bride; you are an enclosed spring, a sealed-up fountain.
NET.13: Your shoots are a royal garden full of pomegranates with choice fruits: henna with nard,
NET.14: nard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon with every kind of spice, myrrh and aloes with all the finest spices.
NET.15: You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water flowing down from Lebanon.
NET.16: Awake, O north wind; come, O south wind! Blow on my garden so that its fragrant spices may send out their sweet smell. May my beloved come into his garden and eat its delightful fruit!
